AURELLE AIR — CUSTOMER RELATIONS, COMPENSATION DESK
Claim file CR-26-08-44187. Documents: (1) Passenger Service Commitment (PSC), edition 2025, as amended by Revision 3; (2) superseded PSC Revision 2 list of extraordinary circumstances (retained in the claim template); (3) Annex D distance table extract; (4) booking and operational records; (5) claim correspondence.

(1) PASSENGER SERVICE COMMITMENT — EDITION 2025 (in force for flights from 1 April 2025), WITH REVISION 3 (in force for flights operated from 1 February 2026)

Part A — General
A1 The PSC is part of Aurelle Air's Conditions of Carriage. It gives passengers rights to care, rerouting, refunds and fixed compensation in the cases described below. It does not limit any rights passengers have under the law of the country of departure.
A2 The PSC applies to passengers holding a confirmed reservation on a flight operated by Aurelle Air, who presented themselves for check-in by the published deadline (or, with online check-in, at the gate by the boarding deadline).
A3 Codeshare flights marketed by Aurelle Air but operated by another airline are handled under the operating airline's conditions.

Part B — Definitions
B1 "Booking" — one or more flights under one booking reference (PNR), ticketed together. Flights booked under separate PNRs are separate Bookings even when the passengers travel together.
B2 "Final Destination" — the destination on the ticket of the last flight of the Booking. Alternative connecting flights taken because of a disruption do not change the Final Destination.
B3 "Arrival Time" — the moment at which at least one door of the aircraft is opened after the aircraft has reached its parking position, passengers being permitted to leave the aircraft. Touchdown time and on-block time are recorded for operational purposes and are not the Arrival Time.
B4 "Arrival Delay" — the difference between the scheduled arrival time at the Final Destination of the Booking and the Arrival Time at the Final Destination, both expressed in the same time reference.
B5 "Distance" — the great-circle distance between the airport of first departure and the Final Destination of the Booking, as listed in Annex D. For Bookings with connections, the distances of the individual flights are not added.
B6 "Extraordinary Circumstances" — the circumstances listed in Part F, which could not have been avoided even if all reasonable measures had been taken.
B7 "Rerouting" — carriage to the Final Destination under comparable conditions at the earliest opportunity, offered by Aurelle Air after a cancellation, denied boarding or missed connection.

Part C — Care
C1 Meals and refreshments in reasonable relation to the waiting time, from 2 hours of expected delay (short flights), 3 hours (medium), 4 hours (long).
C2 Hotel accommodation where an overnight stay becomes necessary.
C3 Care is provided in kind (vouchers) or reimbursed against receipts within reasonable limits.
C4 Passengers are offered two telephone calls or e-mails free of charge.
C5 Care is not refused because the cause of the delay is an Extraordinary Circumstance; E3 limits fixed compensation only.

Part D — Refunds and rerouting
D1 Where a flight is cancelled, or a delay of 5 hours or more is expected, passengers may choose a refund of the unused part of the ticket instead of travel.
D2 A passenger who misses a connection within the same Booking because of a delay of an earlier flight is offered Rerouting.

Part E — Fixed compensation
E1 A passenger whose Arrival Delay at the Final Destination is 3 hours or more receives fixed compensation according to the Distance:
  Distance up to 1,500 km: EUR 250
  Distance more than 1,500 km and up to 3,500 km: EUR 400
  Distance more than 3,500 km: EUR 300 if the Arrival Delay is 3 hours or more but less than 4 hours; EUR 600 if the Arrival Delay is 4 hours or more.
E2 Compensation under E1 is reduced by 50 % where the passenger was offered Rerouting and the Arrival Delay at the Final Destination does not exceed: 2 hours (Distance up to 1,500 km), 3 hours (more than 1,500 up to 3,500 km), 4 hours (more than 3,500 km).
E3 No compensation is payable where the delay or cancellation was caused by Extraordinary Circumstances, or where the passenger was informed of a cancellation at least 14 days before scheduled departure.
E4 Compensation is paid per passenger, in cash, bank transfer or (with the passenger's written agreement) travel vouchers. Infants travelling free of charge on a lap are not entitled to compensation.
E5 Where a delay on an earlier flight of the Booking causes a missed connection, the Arrival Delay at the Final Destination is decisive; the cause of the delay of the earlier flight is examined under E3.
E6 Claims must be made within 2 years of the scheduled date of the flight.

Part F — Extraordinary Circumstances (as amended by Revision 3)
F1 Meteorological conditions incompatible with the safe operation of the flight.
F2 Air traffic management decisions (slot restrictions, airspace closures) and strikes by staff not employed by Aurelle Air or its contractors.
F3 Security risks, political instability, and airport closures ordered by authorities.
F4 Bird strikes and damage to the aircraft caused by third parties (e.g. ground-handling vehicles of other operators).
F5 Hidden manufacturing defects that affect the safety of the flight and that the aircraft manufacturer or an authority has notified to operators.
F6 Revision 3 note: technical problems that arise in connection with the maintenance or operation of the aircraft, including those discovered during routine checks or pre-flight inspections, are not Extraordinary Circumstances unless covered by F5. Staff shortages and strikes by Aurelle Air's own staff are not Extraordinary Circumstances.

Part G — Downgrading
G1 Passengers placed in a lower class than booked receive a refund of 30 % (up to 1,500 km), 50 % (1,500–3,500 km) or 75 % (above 3,500 km) of the ticket price of the affected flight.

Part H — Baggage
H1 Delayed checked baggage: reimbursement of reasonable essential purchases up to EUR 50 per day for up to 5 days, against receipts.
H2 Lost baggage: liability as set out in the Conditions of Carriage, Article 17; claims within 21 days of the date the baggage should have been delivered.
H3 Baggage delays do not give rise to fixed compensation under Part E.

Part I — Claims handling
I1 Claims are assessed per passenger. A claim form may cover several passengers of one Booking; passengers on other Bookings must claim separately.
I2 The desk establishes the facts from the operational log (times in UTC) and converts them to the local time of the relevant airport using the time references in Annex D.
I3 The automatic pre-fill in the claim template is an aid for the desk and is not binding.
I4 Payment is made within 30 days of acceptance of the claim.
I5 Travel agencies may submit claims on behalf of passengers with a signed mandate; payment is then made to the passenger's account unless the mandate says otherwise.

Part J — Passengers with reduced mobility and unaccompanied minors
J1 Passengers with reduced mobility and their companions, and unaccompanied minors, receive care under Part C as soon as possible irrespective of the delay thresholds.
J2 Compensation under Part E is not increased for these passengers.

Part K — Goodwill gestures
K1 Customer Relations may offer vouchers as a goodwill gesture where no compensation is due. Goodwill vouchers are not compensation under Part E and are not offset against it.
K2 Where compensation under Part E is paid, meal vouchers and hotel costs under Part C are not deducted.
K3 Where a passenger accepts a voucher under E4 instead of cash, the voucher value is 130 % of the cash amount.

(2) SUPERSEDED — PSC REVISION 2, PART F (flights operated 1 April 2025 – 31 January 2026), as printed in the claim template

  Pre-flight inspection by Aurelle Air engineers at PVL found a hydraulic fluid leak at the left main landing-gear actuator; a seal was replaced. No manufacturer or authority notice applied to the part. Departure 12:57 local (72 minutes late); arrival DRN 17:14 local (69 minutes late).
  Ground handling at PVL was provided by Portavela Ground Services, whose staff were not on strike. The PVL tower reported no slot restrictions for AU 311.

Last A-check 2 August 2026, no findings. No airworthiness directive or service bulletin applicable to P/N 42-7719-03." HARWOOD METROPOLITAN UNIVERSITY — ACADEMIC REGISTRY, APPEALS OFFICE
Admissibility screening: appeal APL-2027-0038
Documents in this file: (1) Academic Appeals Regulations (AAR), 2025/26 edition, as amended by Senate Resolution S/2026/41; (2) Academic Calendar 2026/27 extract; (3) Student Complaints Procedure extract (for reference in cases transferred between procedures); (4) student record extracts; (5) the appeal submission and related correspondence.

(1) ACADEMIC APPEALS REGULATIONS, 2025/26 EDITION

Section 1 — Interpretation
1.1 These Regulations apply to appeals against decisions of Boards of Examiners and of Progression Boards on taught programmes.
1.2 "Student" includes a person whose registration ended within the previous six months.
1.3 "Result" means a decision of a Board of Examiners or Progression Board recorded on the student record: a module mark, a progression decision, or an award and classification decision.
1.4 "Working day" means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays in England and the University closure days listed in the Academic Calendar. Days on which teaching does not take place (reading weeks, vacations) are working days unless they are closure days.
1.5 "Publication" of a Result means its release to the student on the Student Portal. E-mail notifications that a Result is available are courtesy messages and do not affect the date of Publication.
1.6 Periods expressed in working days run from the working day following the event that starts them. A period ends at 23:59 UK time on its last working day.
1.7 "Lodged" means received through the Appeals form (AP1) on the Student Portal. Where the Student Portal is unavailable for more than four hours on the last day of a period, an appeal e-mailed to appeals@harwood-met.example on that day is treated as lodged.

Section 2 — Who may appeal
2.1 Any Student may appeal against a Result that affects them.
2.2 An appeal may not be made by a third party except with the student's written consent.
2.3 A student who has attended a graduation ceremony and accepted the award to which the appeal relates may not appeal against the classification of that award.

Section 3 — Time limits
3.1 An appeal must be lodged within 10 working days of Publication of the Result.
3.2 An appeal lodged out of time is not admissible unless the student shows, with independent evidence, that they were prevented from lodging it in time by circumstances beyond their control; in that case it must be lodged within 5 working days after those circumstances ended.
3.3 Time limits are not extended because a student is awaiting the outcome of an informal discussion, a request for feedback or a request for a re-count of marks, unless the Appeals Office agreed an extension in writing before the time limit expired.

Section 4 — Grounds
4.1 An appeal may be made only on one or more of the following grounds:
  (a) a material procedural irregularity in the conduct of the assessment or of the Board's decision, which may have affected the Result;
  (b) circumstances affecting the student's performance which, for good reason, the student was unable to disclose before the Board met;
  (c) evidence of prejudice or bias, or of a reasonable perception of bias, on the part of an examiner.
4.2 Disagreement with the academic judgement of examiners is not a ground of appeal. Academic judgement includes the marks awarded, the assessment of the quality of work and the application of marking criteria.
4.3 An appeal which includes matters outside 4.1 is admissible in respect of those grounds that fall within 4.1; the other matters are struck out at screening.
4.4 An appeal consisting only of matters outside 4.1 is not admissible.

Section 5 — Stage 1 (informal resolution)
5.1 Before lodging an appeal, a student must first raise the matter with the Programme Leader (Stage 1) and allow five working days for a response. The Stage 1 outcome or the expiry of five working days without a response must be recorded on the AP1 form.
5.2 Stage 1 does not apply where the appeal is against an award and classification decision of a Board of Examiners, or where the matter concerns the conduct of the Programme Leader.
5.3 Raising a matter under Stage 1 does not stop the time limit in Section 3 running.

Section 6 — Evidence
6.1 Documentary evidence should accompany the AP1 form. Evidence not available when the appeal is lodged may be submitted within 10 working days after lodging.
6.2 Medical evidence must be from a registered practitioner and must cover the relevant dates.

Section 7 — Screening and outcomes
7.1 The Appeals Office screens each appeal for admissibility (Sections 2–5) within 10 working days of lodging.
7.2 Admissible appeals are referred to an Appeals Panel. Inadmissible appeals receive a Completion of Procedures letter.

Section 8 — Appeals Panel
8.1 An Appeals Panel consists of a chair from the Senate, an academic from another faculty and, where the student requests it, a student member nominated by the Students' Union.
8.2 The Panel considers the written submission, the evidence and the response of the Board of Examiners. The student may attend and be accompanied by a friend or a Students' Union adviser.
8.3 The Panel may (a) dismiss the appeal; (b) refer the matter back to the Board of Examiners for reconsideration, with directions; (c) where the ground in 4.1(a) is upheld, direct that the student be offered a further attempt at the affected assessment without penalty.
8.4 The Panel does not substitute its own academic judgement for that of the examiners.

Section 9 — Completion of procedures
9.1 A Completion of Procedures letter is issued at the end of the internal process. The student may then take the matter to the independent external reviewer within 12 months.
9.2 A student whose appeal is found inadmissible at screening may ask the Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Education) to review the screening decision within 5 working days of the decision.

Section 10 — Records and confidentiality
10.1 Appeal files are retained for six years after the Completion of Procedures letter.
10.2 Information provided in an appeal is shared only with those who need it to consider the appeal.

Section 11 — Appeals against progression decisions (Progression Boards)
11.1 A student required to resit or repeat may appeal under these Regulations. Stage 1 applies to all progression appeals.

======================================================================
A. ENTERPRISE LICENCE AGREEMENT TES-ELA-2023-118 (signed 1 March 2023) — EXTRACTS
======================================================================
1. Definitions
1.1 "Software" — Tessellate CAD Enterprise, including the desktop client, the web viewer and the rendering server components.
1.2 "Licence" — a named-user subscription licence to use the Software. One Licence permits one Named User to use the Software on any number of devices.
1.3 "Licensee Affiliates" — entities controlling, controlled by or under common control with the Licensee; their use counts as the Licensee's use.
1.4 "Named User" — an individual human being who is authorised by the Licensee to access the Software and has an active account on the Measurement Date. An individual is one Named User regardless of how many accounts the individual holds.
1.5 Shared accounts. Where an account is used by more than one individual, each individual who used that account during the three months ending on the Measurement Date is a Named User. The Licensee shall keep login records sufficient to identify such individuals.
1.6 Service accounts. An account used solely by software processes through the rendering-server API, without interactive login, is a "Service Account" and is not a Named User. If an individual logs in interactively through a Service Account at any time during the three months ending on the Measurement Date, that individual is a Named User.
1.7 "Active account" — any account that exists on the Measurement Date, unless it was disabled or deleted at least 30 days before the Measurement Date.
1.8 "Measurement Date" — 31 August of each year of the term.
1.9 "Production Environment" — any installation of the Software other than a registered Non-Production Environment (see Amendment No. 2).

2. Grant of licence and restrictions
2.1 Tessellate grants the Licensee a non-exclusive, non-transferable right to use the Software during the term for its internal business purposes, up to the number of Licences held.
2.2 The Licensee shall not (a) sublicense, rent or lease the Software; (b) use the Software to provide design services to third parties other than its own customers under contracts for vessels designed or built by the Licensee; (c) circumvent licence controls.
2.3 The Software may be installed in any country in which the Licensee or its Licensee Affiliates operate, subject to export control laws.
2.4 Plug-ins developed by the Licensee using the Tessellate SDK may be used without additional licences, but each individual using them requires a Licence as a Named User.

3. Use by third parties
3.1 The Licensee may permit its contractors and outsourcing providers to use the Software solely for the Licensee's internal business purposes.
3.2 Contractors and outsourcing providers who use the Software under 3.1 are Named Users of the Licensee and require Licences, unless the contractor uses the contractor's own Tessellate licences under the contractor's own agreement and the Licensee has received written confirmation of this from Tessellate.
3.3 The Licensee is responsible for the compliance of such third parties.

4. Fees
4.1 Subscription fees are invoiced annually in advance on 1 March for all Licences held.
4.2 Licences added during a subscription year are invoiced pro rata from their licence start date to the next 1 March.
4.3 List price for 2026: EUR 2,340 per Licence per year.

5. True-up
5.1 Each year the Licensee reports the number of Named Users as of the Measurement Date.
5.2 The number of Licences held on the Measurement Date is the number of Licences under all Order Forms whose licence start date is on or before the Measurement Date.
5.3 If the number of Named Users exceeds the number of Licences held, the Licensee purchases the shortfall at the then-current list price, with back-dated subscription fees for 12 months.
5.4 A true-up shortfall of more than 15 Licences, or of more than 10 % of Licences held, entitles Tessellate to conduct an audit at the Licensee's expense.

6. Audit
6.1 Tessellate may audit the Licensee's use of the Software once per year on 30 days' notice, in addition to any audit under 5.4.
6.2 The Licensee shall provide login records, identity management exports and Order Forms on request.
6.3 If an audit reveals a shortfall that the Licensee did not report in its True-Up Report, the Licensee pays the shortfall at 125 % of list price.

7. Term
7.1 The ELA runs until 28 February 2028 and may be renewed for further five-year terms.

8. Support and maintenance
8.1 Support is included in the subscription fee. Support cases may be raised by up to five designated contacts of the Licensee.
8.2 New releases are made available to all Licences held; the Licensee may continue to use the previous major release for 12 months after a new major release.

9. Data protection
9.1 Login records processed by Tessellate for licence management are processed as a processor on behalf of the Licensee; they are deleted 24 months after collection.

======================================================================
B. AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
Amendment No. 1 (signed 12 February 2024)
B1.1 Named Users who, on the Measurement Date, have been on continuous leave of absence (parental, sick, sabbatical) for 90 days or more, and whose accounts were not used during that leave, are not counted as Named Users for that Measurement Date.

LATTICEPAY PLATFORM — INCIDENT MANAGEMENT
Post-incident severity review for INC-2026-0908-114 ("Invoice API elevated 5xx, eu-west")
Pack contents: (A) Incident Severity Runbook ISR, version 5.0, with Change Notice CN-5.1; (B) Security Incident Classification Standard SICS-2 (extract); (C) glossary extract from the Platform Handbook; (D) incident timeline and monitoring data; (E) customer impact data; (F) on-call notes.

======================================================================
(A) INCIDENT SEVERITY RUNBOOK ISR v5.0 (effective 1 February 2026)
======================================================================
1. Purpose
1.1 The severity of an incident determines paging, communication cadence, executive notification and the post-incident review format. The final severity is set at the post-incident review according to this runbook, based on the facts established after the incident; the severity declared during the incident is provisional.
1.2 This runbook covers availability, performance and data incidents. Security incidents (suspected or confirmed unauthorised access, data exfiltration, credential compromise) are classified under SICS-2 instead; where an incident is both, the higher of the two severities applies.

2. Definitions
2.1 "Active tenant" — a tenant that sent at least one API request in the 7 days before the incident started.
2.2 "Affected tenant" — an active tenant for which more than 5 % of its API requests failed (5xx or timeout) in at least one 10-minute monitoring window during the incident. Tenants with some failed requests below that rate in every window are not affected tenants.
2.3 "Enterprise tenant" — a tenant on an Enterprise plan with a signed Enterprise Master Services Agreement. Tenants on an Enterprise Trial (evaluation) plan are not Enterprise tenants for the purposes of this runbook.
2.4 "Payment processing" — the authorisation, capture, refund and payout APIs, and the ledger writes behind them. Invoicing, billing documents (invoice PDFs, statements), reporting and the merchant dashboard are not payment processing.
2.5 "Incident duration" — the time from the start of the first 10-minute monitoring window in which the incident's failure criterion was met to the end of the last such window. Alerting, acknowledgement and verification times are not part of the incident duration.
2.6 "Workaround" — a documented alternative that allows affected tenants to complete the affected operation without LatticePay intervention (e.g. a fallback endpoint), communicated to them on the status page or directly.
2.7 "Data loss" — loss of data that LatticePay had acknowledged as received. Data that can be restored automatically from the write-ahead log or replayed from the event archive, without manual reconstruction and with no more than 15 minutes of data affected, is "recoverable within RPO".

3. Base severity (impact)
3.1 SEV-1: more than 40 % of active tenants affected; or any unrecoverable data loss; or complete unavailability of payment processing in any region for 5 minutes or more.
3.2 SEV-2: more than 10 % and up to 40 % of active tenants affected; or 3 or more Enterprise tenants affected.
3.3 SEV-3: at least 1 % and up to 10 % of active tenants affected; or 1 or 2 Enterprise tenants affected.
3.4 SEV-4: fewer than 1 % of active tenants affected and no Enterprise tenant affected.
3.5 Where several criteria apply, the highest resulting severity is the base severity.

4. Adjustments (applied to the base severity in this order)
4.1 Duration: if the incident duration is more than 4 hours, raise the severity by one level (SEV-4 → SEV-3, SEV-3 → SEV-2, SEV-2 → SEV-1).
4.2 Workaround: if a Workaround was available to all affected tenants for the whole incident duration after the first 30 minutes, lower the severity by one level.
4.3 An adjustment never moves the severity above SEV-1 or below SEV-4.

5. Communication by severity
5.1 SEV-1: status page within 15 minutes; updates every 30 minutes; executive on-call paged; customer RCA within 5 business days.
5.2 SEV-2: status page within 30 minutes; updates hourly; customer RCA within 10 business days.
5.3 SEV-3: status page if more than 20 tenants affected; internal review only.
5.4 SEV-4: no status page; ticket-level follow-up.

6. Roles
6.1 Incident commander (IC): declares provisional severity, coordinates responders.
6.2 Communications lead: status page and Enterprise account managers.
6.3 Scribe: timeline in the incident channel.
6.4 Service owner: confirms the technical facts used for the final severity (affected tenants, duration, data impact) in writing before the review.
6.5 The IC's provisional severity is not changed during the incident for reclassification purposes; reclassification happens only at the review.

7. Post-incident review
7.1 A post-incident review is held within 5 business days for SEV-1 and SEV-2 incidents and within 15 business days for SEV-3. SEV-4 incidents are reviewed in the weekly operations meeting.
7.2 The review records the final severity, the facts on which it is based and the corrective actions.
7.3 Final severity drives the reliability scorecard: SEV-1 = 10 points, SEV-2 = 5, SEV-3 = 2, SEV-4 = 0.

8. Historical note
8.1 ISR v4.2 (in force until 31 January 2026) used "tenants with any failed request" as affected tenants and treated Enterprise Trial tenants as Enterprise tenants. It had no workaround adjustment and no floors.

Appendix — Recent final severities (for consistency checks)
INC-2026-0114-021 | ISR v4.2 | 212 of 3,870 tenants with any failure (5.5 %) | 1 Enterprise | SEV-3
INC-2026-0322-067 | ISR v5.0 | 44 affected of 3,950 (1.1 %) | 0 Enterprise | 2 h 10 min | Workaround from 00:12 | SEV-4
INC-2026-0611-088 | ISR v5.0 + CN-5.1 | Payouts API degraded 22 min, 0.8 % affected | SEV-2 (payment processing floor)
INC-2026-0729-102 | ISR v5.0 + CN-5.1 | 9.4 % affected | 1 Enterprise | 4 h 30 min | SEV-2 (duration raise)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
CHANGE NOTICE CN-5.1 (approved by the Reliability Council, effective 1 June 2026)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
CN-5.1.1 New section 4.4: "Floor for Enterprise impact. After the adjustments in 4.1 and 4.2, an incident in which at least one Enterprise tenant was affected is never below SEV-3."
CN-5.1.2 New section 3.6: "Payment processing floor. Any incident in which payment processing was degraded (more than 5 % failed requests in a 10-minute window) for 15 minutes or more is at least SEV-2 before adjustments."
CN-5.1.3 Section 2.7 is amended by adding: "Data that is recoverable only by manual reconstruction, or where more than 15 minutes of data is affected, is recoverable but not within RPO; such an incident is at least SEV-2 before adjustments."
CN-5.1.4 Section 5.3 is amended: status page for SEV-3 if more than 10 tenants affected.

======================================================================
(B) SECURITY INCIDENT CLASSIFICATION STANDARD SICS-2 — EXTRACT
======================================================================
S1 Any confirmed unauthorised access to cardholder data: S-1 (maps to SEV-1).
S2 Suspected unauthorised access under investigation: S-2 (maps to SEV-2) until closed.
S3 Vulnerability discovered without evidence of exploitation: S-3 (maps to SEV-3).
S4 A security review opened as routine follow-up to an availability incident, where no unauthorised access is suspected, is not a security incident.

======================================================================
(C) PLATFORM HANDBOOK — GLOSSARY EXTRACT
======================================================================
Invoice API — generates invoice documents (PDF/UBL) for merchants' customers and stores them in the document store. Part of the Billing Documents product.
Payments API — authorisation, capture, refund; Payouts API — merchant settlements.
Webhook dispatcher — delivers event notifications to tenants; events are persisted in the event archive for 30 days and can be replayed automatically.
Regions: eu-west (primary for EU tenants), eu-central (DR).

======================================================================
(D) INCIDENT TIMELINE (UTC) AND MONITORING
======================================================================
8 September 2026
13:31 Deployment of document-store client library 4.12.0 to Invoice API pods in eu-west.
13:40–13:50 First 10-minute monitoring window in which the Invoice API 5xx rate exceeded 5 % for affected tenants.
13:41 Alert "invoice-api 5xx > 2 %" fired; on-call acknowledged 13:44.
13:52 IC declared provisional SEV-2 ("wide customer impact, cause unknown, payments?").
14:05 Payments API, Payouts API: error rates checked — normal (0.02 %); no degradation of authorisation, capture or refund at any time during the incident.
14:08 Workaround published on the status page and sent to all tenants with failed requests: "Use the v1 invoice endpoint /v1/invoices/render (synchronous) until further notice." The v1 endpoint remained fully available throughout.
14:47 Webhook dispatcher backlog; 11 minutes of "invoice.rendered" events (14:36–14:47) dropped from the in-memory queue during a pod restart.
15:10 Event replay from the event archive started automatically for 14:36–14:47; completed 15:18; no manual steps.
16:55 Rollback to library 4.11.3 started.
17:30–17:40 Last 10-minute monitoring window with 5xx rate above 5 %.
17:51 IC declared all-clear after verification.
Security: on 9 September a routine security review ticket SEC-REV-2231 was opened "as standard follow-up to any library-related incident"; no unauthorised access suspected; closed 11 September with no findings.

======================================================================
(E) CUSTOMER IMPACT DATA (analytics export, 10 September 2026)
======================================================================
Active tenants (at least one request in the 7 days before 13:31 on 8 September): 4,020. Provisioned tenants (all, including dormant): 5,610.
Tenants with at least one failed Invoice API request during the incident: 455.
Tenants with more than 5 % of API requests failed in at least one 10-minute window: 318.
Enterprise-plan tenants among the 318:
  T-10044 Moravia Retail Group — Enterprise plan, Enterprise MSA signed 2023.
  T-11820 Kestrel Hospitality — Enterprise plan, Enterprise MSA signed March 2026.
  T-12977 Orinoco Sports GmbH — Enterprise Trial plan (evaluation until 30 September 2026); MSA under negotiation.
Enterprise-plan tenants among the 137 tenants with failures below 5 % in every window: T-10390 Harwell Foods (Enterprise, MSA 2024).
Payments API volume during the incident: normal; no tenant had payment failures above baseline.

======================================================================
(F) ON-CALL NOTES
======================================================================
IC handover note (18:05): "Total impact roughly 4 h 10 min from first alert to all-clear. Three Enterprise customers affected, 455 tenants saw errors. Webhook events lost for 11 min but replayed. Suggest keeping SEV-2 for the review."
Communications lead: status page updates posted 14:02, 14:08, 15:00, 16:00, 17:00, 17:55. Account managers of T-10044, T-11820 and T-12977 informed.
Root-cause summary (engineering, 10 September): "Library 4.12.0 changed the default connection-pool size for the document store from 64 to 8. Under normal afternoon load, render requests queued and timed out after 30 s, returning 504. The synchronous v1 endpoint uses a separate pool and was unaffected. The in-memory webhook queue lost events on the pod restart at 14:47 because the graceful-shutdown hook was also affected; the archive-based replay worked as designed."
Corrective actions proposed: pin pool size in configuration; canary deployments for library upgrades; alert threshold review.
Reliability Council note (review agenda for 15 September): INC-2026-0908-114 — final severity to be determined per ISR v5.0 as amended.

options: 0: SEV-4 (lowest)
1: SEV-3
2: SEV-2
3: SEV-1 (highest)

(1) COMMERCIAL RETURNS POLICY CRP-5

§1 Scope

1.2 Warranty claims under the Corvid Limited Warranty (24 months) are handled separately by the Service department; a return under CRP-5 is a commercial return (return for credit) and does not affect warranty rights.

§2 Definitions
2.1 "Standard Product" — a product listed in the Corvid catalogue, supplied in a catalogue configuration.
2.2 "Custom-built Product" — a product built to the customer's specification, including any product whose configuration was not available in the catalogue, products with customer-specific firmware, labelling or housings, and products ordered under a project quotation.
2.3 "Delivery Date" — the date on which the goods were delivered to the customer's delivery address, as shown by the carrier's proof of delivery. The dispatch date and the invoice date are not the Delivery Date.
2.4 "RMA Request Date" — the date on which the customer submits a complete return request in the Corvid partner portal (order number, items, quantities and reason).
2.5 "Defective" — a product in which Corvid's inspection confirms a fault in materials or workmanship present at delivery. A product returned as defective in which the inspection finds no fault ("No Fault Found", NFF) is not Defective.
2.6 "Unused" — not installed in a powered application for more than 72 hours in total, with no physical damage, and returned with all accessories.

§3 Return window and eligibility
3.1 Standard Products may be returned for credit if the RMA Request Date is no later than 30 days after the Delivery Date and the products are Unused, or are Defective.
3.2 Custom-built Products are not returnable for credit. Defective Custom-built Products are repaired or replaced under 5.3.
3.3 Returns of Standard Products requested more than 30 days after the Delivery Date are rejected, unless the products are Defective (5.3 applies).
3.4 Minimum return value: EUR 100 per RMA.

§4 Credit
4.1 Returns accepted under 3.1 are credited at the invoiced net price.
4.2 A restocking fee of 15 % of the credited value is deducted for returns that are not Defective.
4.3 The restocking fee is waived (a) for Gold partners; (b) where the return results from a Corvid shipping or order-entry error; (c) for products discontinued by Corvid within 60 days before the RMA Request Date.
4.4 Freight for returns that are not Defective is paid by the customer.
4.5 No restocking fee may be waived other than under 4.3, except with the written approval of the Head of Customer Service.
4.6 Credits are calculated per RMA; partial returns of an order line are credited pro rata.

§5 Defective products
5.1 Products returned as Defective are inspected within 10 business days of receipt.
5.2 Defective Standard Products returned within the 30-day window are credited in full (no restocking fee); outside the window they are repaired or replaced.
5.3 Defective Custom-built Products are repaired or replaced; no credit is given.
5.4 NFF returns are treated as returns that are not Defective. Eligibility and credit are assessed under §3 and §4 as at the RMA Request Date.

§6 Process
6.1 Goods must not be sent back without an RMA number.
6.2 The returns desk issues its decision (credit with or without fee, repair/replace, or rejection) after inspection.
6.3 Goods returned without an RMA number, or more than 15 days after the RMA number was issued, may be refused at the warehouse.
6.4 The customer bears the risk of loss in transit for returns that are not Defective.

§7 Special cases
7.1 Demonstration units lent to customers are not sales and are returned under the loan agreement.
7.2 Trade-in programme: customers replacing CX-200 controllers with CX-400 controllers may return the old units for a trade-in credit of EUR 150 per unit within 90 days of the CX-400 delivery; trade-ins are not returns under CRP-5.
7.3 Software licences and firmware upgrade keys are not returnable once activated.
7.4 Spare parts ordered through the Service department are returned under the Service terms.

§8 Credit notes
8.1 Credit notes are issued in the currency of the original invoice within 10 business days of the returns desk decision.
8.2 Credit notes are offset against open invoices first; any balance is paid out on request.
8.3 Restocking fees are shown as a separate line on the credit note.

§9 Returns from outside the EU
9.1 Customers outside the EU must return goods with export documentation marking them as returned goods; customs duties charged on re-import are deducted from the credit unless the return is Defective.
9.2 Norway: returns are processed with a T1 transit document; no import duty is charged on returned Corvid goods of EU origin if the documentation is correct.

§10 Relationship with the Limited Warranty
10.1 A customer whose return request is rejected under §3 keeps any warranty rights for Defective products.
10.2 Products found NFF under a warranty claim are returned to the customer at the customer's cost; an inspection fee of EUR 60 per unit may be charged under the Service terms.

TIDEMARK GROUP — PEOPLE OPERATIONS (UK)
Sabbatical application review: SAB-APP-2026-0219
Pack: (1) Sabbatical Leave Policy SAB-2 (issued 1 March 2024) with Amendment 2026/1; (2) Continuity of Service Guideline CSG-1 (extracts); (3) Career Break Policy CB-1 (extract, for comparison); (4) employee records; (5) application and manager's endorsement.

(1) SABBATICAL LEAVE POLICY SAB-2

1. Purpose
1.1 Sabbatical leave gives long-serving employees a period of paid leave for rest, study or voluntary work. It is granted once in any seven-year period.

2. Definitions
2.1 "Employer" — the Tidemark Group company that employs the employee on the date of application.
2.2 "Qualifying Service" — service counted in accordance with the Continuity of Service Guideline CSG-1, as at the day before the requested sabbatical start date.
2.3 "Year" — for the purposes of this policy, a period of 365 days of Qualifying Service. Qualifying Service is counted in calendar days.
2.4 "Grade" — the employee's grade in the Tidemark grading structure (E1 to E9).
2.5 "Performance rating" — the rating from the annual performance cycle (Outstanding, Strong, Meets, Partly meets, Does not meet).

3. Eligibility
3.1 An employee is eligible for sabbatical leave if, on the requested sabbatical start date:
  (a) the employee has at least five Years of Qualifying Service;
  (b) the employee's two most recent completed performance ratings are "Meets" or better;
  (c) the employee is not subject to a formal performance improvement plan or a live disciplinary warning; and
  (d) the employee has not taken a sabbatical in the previous seven years.
3.2 The application must be submitted at least three months before the requested start date.
3.3 The employee's line manager must endorse the application; the manager may propose a different start date for business reasons, but may not refuse an eligible application more than once.

4. Duration and pay
4.1 Sabbatical leave is four weeks on full pay, which may be combined with up to four weeks of annual leave.
4.2 During sabbatical leave, all contractual benefits continue.
4.3 Sabbatical pay is calculated on basic salary only; allowances for on-call or shift work are not included.

5. Return
5.1 An employee who resigns within six months of returning from sabbatical repays the sabbatical pay.
5.2 On return, the employee resumes the same role on the same terms.
5.3 An employee may be asked to share what they learned during a study sabbatical with their team.

6. Process
6.1 Applications are submitted through the HR portal (form SAB-A) with the requested start date, duration and purpose.
6.2 People Operations checks eligibility within 15 working days and informs the employee and manager of the outcome.
6.3 Where People Operations finds the employee not yet eligible, it states the earliest date on which the employee would become eligible, and the employee may re-apply for a start date on or after that date without further delay beyond 3.2.
6.4 Approved sabbaticals may be postponed once by the employee, by up to six months, without re-application.

7. Interaction with other leave
7.1 Sabbatical leave cannot be combined with unpaid leave or a career break under CB-1.
7.2 If the employee falls ill during sabbatical leave, the sabbatical is not extended.
7.3 Public holidays falling within sabbatical leave are part of the sabbatical.

8. Appeals
8.1 An employee may appeal against a refusal to the Head of People Operations within 10 working days. The appeal is decided on the policy as written; discretionary exceptions are not available.

AMENDMENT 2026/1 (approved by the Group People Committee, effective 1 January 2026)
A1 Section 3.1(a) is replaced by: "(a) the employee has at least five Years of Qualifying Service or, if the employee is in Grade E5 or above on the requested sabbatical start date, at least four Years of Qualifying Service;".
A2 Section 3.2: applications for start dates in December require four months' notice.
A3 The amendment applies to applications submitted on or after 1 January 2026.

(2) CONTINUITY OF SERVICE GUIDELINE CSG-1 — EXTRACTS
C1 Qualifying Service is continuous employment with the Employer, counted from the start date of the current period of employment.
C2 Transfers within the group: where an employee transfers from one Tidemark Group company to another without any break between the two employments, service with the previous company counts as service with the Employer.
C3 Re-hire: where a former employee is re-hired by the same company within six months after the end of the previous employment, the previous period of employment is added to Qualifying Service (the gap between the employments does not count). Re-hire by a different Tidemark Group company does not reinstate the previous period.
C4 Paid leave of any kind, including statutory maternity, paternity, adoption and shared parental leave while paid, and sickness absence, counts as Qualifying Service.
C5 Unpaid leave: a single continuous period of unpaid leave of 90 days or fewer counts as Qualifying Service. A single continuous period of unpaid leave of more than 90 days does not break continuity, but the whole of that period is excluded from Qualifying Service.
C6 Secondments to external organisations with a right to return count as Qualifying Service.
C7 Periods on a zero-hours or casual contract with a group company before a permanent contract do not count.
C8 Periods of notice worked count; periods of garden leave count.
C9 Service with a company acquired by the group counts from the date of acquisition unless the acquisition agreement provides otherwise.
C10 Industrial action days: excluded but do not break continuity.
C11 Where an employee's contract is transferred by operation of law into a group company, service with the transferor counts.
C12 Calculation example (days): an employee who started on 1 July 2021 and has a single unpaid leave of 30 days has, on 30 June 2025, 1,461 days of employment, all of which count.

(3) CAREER BREAK POLICY CB-1 — EXTRACT (for comparison; not applicable to sabbatical leave)
CB 2.1 Employees with three years of service may take an unpaid career break of 3 to 24 months. For the purposes of CB-1, service is counted from the first date of employment with any Tidemark Group company, including earlier periods of employment if re-hired within 12 months.
CB 2.2 Career breaks do not count as service for any purpose.

(4) EMPLOYEE RECORDS

    Grade: E4 until 30 September 2026; E5 from 1 October 2026 (promotion letter dated 12 August 2026).

  Record B — Marta Rinaldi, employee no. TA-07712, Tidemark Analytics Ltd, Grade E6, continuous employment since 3 April 2018; sabbatical taken 2025.

(5) APPLICATION
Application SAB-APP-2026-0219 submitted 15 September 2026 by employee no. TA-10388: "Requested sabbatical: four weeks from Monday 1 February 2027, combined with two weeks of annual leave; purpose: completing a data-science certificate."

Pension scheme record (Tidemark Group Pension Plan): pensionable service from 15 August 2022; contributions suspended 1 June – 22 November 2024.

(6) GROUP COMPANIES AND REORGANISATION NOTICE
Tidemark Group companies (UK): Tidemark Holdings plc; Tidemark Analytics Ltd; Tidemark Data Services Ltd (dissolved 30 June 2024 after the reorganisation); Tidemark Cloud Operations Ltd; Tidemark Insights Ltd (acquired 1 May 2023).
Reorganisation notice RN-2023-11 (issued 6 November 2023): "With effect from 1 January 2024 all employees of Tidemark Data Services Ltd transfer to Tidemark Analytics Ltd on their existing terms. Continuous service with Tidemark Data Services Ltd is preserved for all purposes. Employee numbers change from TDS- to TA-."
Recruitment file TDS-2231 (Tidemark Data Services Ltd, 2022): "External candidate (previously employed by Tidemark Analytics Ltd until 30.06.2022). Offer 28.07.2022, start 15.08.2022. Probation 6 months."

(7) GRADING STRUCTURE — EXTRACT
E1–E3: associate and analyst roles. E4: senior analyst / senior engineer. E5: lead / principal individual contributor, or team manager. E6–E7: senior manager, head of function. E8–E9: director and executive.
Promotions take effect on the date stated in the promotion letter. Grade changes are recorded in the HR system on their effective date.

(8) SUPERSEDED — SABBATICAL POLICY SAB-1 (1 January 2019 – 29 February 2024), EXTRACT
"S1.1 Eligibility: seven years' continuous service with any Tidemark Group company, counted from the first day of employment; breaks of up to 12 months are bridged. S1.2 Sabbatical: up to eight weeks, of which four weeks paid. S1.3 Unpaid leave counts as service."

(9) CORRESPONDENCE ON THE 2024 LEAVE
Letter from the line manager to the employee, 20 May 2024: "I'm happy to agree your request to extend your leave as unpaid parental leave from 1 June 2024, returning on Monday 25 November 2024. During this period you remain employed; your pension contributions and holiday accrual are suspended."
Letter from People Operations, 22 May 2024: "Your unpaid parental leave 1 June – 22 November 2024 has been recorded (code UPL). It does not break your continuous employment."

(10) SAB-2 FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (intranet, March 2024)
Q: Can I work for another employer during my sabbatical? A: No. Voluntary work for a registered charity is allowed.
Q: Can I split my sabbatical into two periods? A: No, sabbatical leave is taken as one continuous period.
Q: Does sickness absence count towards my service? A: Yes, see CSG-1 C4.
Q: I work part-time. Is my sabbatical shorter? A: No, it is four weeks; pay is at your contractual rate.
Q: Can my manager refuse? A: Only once, for business reasons, if you are eligible (3.3).
Q: When will I hear back? A: Within 15 working days of your application (6.2).
Q: Does a sabbatical affect my bonus? A: No; bonus eligibility is assessed under the Bonus Plan, and sabbatical leave counts as time worked for bonus pro-rating.
Q: Can I take a sabbatical immediately after returning from parental leave? A: Yes, if you are eligible; there is no minimum period back at work.

Morrow Books — fulfillment-control extract, revision 6. Section 2 assigns exception levels: 0 means no operative exception; 1 means requested but unauthorized; 2 means authorized but unused; 3 means used for a shipment. Section 4 says an authorization may be withdrawn until the warehouse first relies on it by bypassing validation or releasing the parcel. Section 7 says packing notes are evidentiary only: copying an authorization does not itself constitute reliance, and a note copied after withdrawal does not restore authority. A portal address correction processed normally is not use of an exception.

Case 44: On 3 May a supervisor authorized one address override. At 08:15 on 4 May the customer corrected the address through the ordinary portal. At 08:22 the supervisor wrote, “Withdraw the override; standard address validation now applies.” At 08:31 a clerk, working from yesterday's queue, copied the authorization into the packing note and marked “override ready.” The validation log at 08:44 shows the corrected address passed standard validation; bypass_used=false. The parcel remains in the cage. A shift summary calls the order “authorized for override,” but it was generated from packing-note text rather than the authority register.

options: 0: No operative exception.

Bright Orchard support handbook, sections 5–8. A ticket may close when the customer reports the affected function working after remediation. An advance statement such as “if X fixes it, close” records conditional consent, not a report that X worked. Agent telemetry can corroborate a customer report but cannot replace one for an interface-visible defect. If reports conflict, evidence about the customer's affected interface outranks backend health; automated summaries never establish customer confirmation.

Ticket BO-771 concerns a dashboard that renders blank for the customer. At 10:02 the customer wrote, “If resetting the gateway fixes it, you can close this.” The agent reset it at 10:14. Gateway telemetry was normal from 10:16 through 11:16, and an automated card displayed RESOLUTION LIKELY. At 11:18 the agent wrote “Reset worked, closing as authorized.” At 11:23 the customer replied from the affected account, “The dashboard is still blank for me. Please do not close.” A synthetic test at 11:25 loaded the dashboard, but no later customer report exists.

TRAVEL REIMBURSEMENT MANUAL — revision 7
1. Purpose and order of authority. This manual governs employee travel reimbursements submitted from 1 April 2026. Defined terms in section 2 apply everywhere, including appendices. If a case-specific written pre-approval conflicts with the standard limits, the pre-approval controls only where section 6 permits it. Amendment A at the end was adopted later than all numbered sections and controls any inconsistency.

2. Definitions. A "travel day" is a calendar day on which the employee is away from the home work location at midnight, except the departure day is also a travel day even when departure is after midnight local time due to a delayed carrier. A "provided meal" is food included without separately stated cost in lodging, conference registration, or carrier service; dietary unsuitability does not stop it being provided unless the accessibility office documented the restriction before travel. "Remote-site travel" means the destination is more than 80 road kilometers from both the employee's home and assigned office. "Timely" means received in the expense portal within 20 business days after the final travel day. Business days exclude weekends and the company closure dates listed in section 9.

3. Meal allowance. The standard allowance is 68 credits per full travel day. Departure and return days receive 75 percent. Deduct 20 percent for a provided breakfast, 30 percent for lunch, and 50 percent for dinner; percentages are of the unadjusted 68-credit daily allowance. The daily result cannot be below zero. Receipts neither increase nor decrease this allowance.

4. Lodging. Lodging is reimbursable up to 190 credits per night. Taxes stated separately are outside that cap. A conference hotel may be reimbursed up to 240 credits only when the booking was made before the conference block closed and the conference organizer named that hotel. Personal upgrades are never reimbursable.

5. Ground transport. Rail is preferred. A taxi over 55 credits requires either a transit-disruption record or remote-site travel. A manager's convenience statement is not a disruption record.

6. Pre-approval. A director may pre-approve lodging above the standard cap or taxi use without a disruption. The writing must identify the trip and a maximum amount. Pre-approval cannot waive timeliness, turn a personal upgrade into business expense, alter meal deductions, or override a later amendment.

7. Late claims. Finance must reject an untimely claim unless the portal was unavailable for at least four continuous hours on the submission deadline and the employee submitted by noon on the next business day. Manager absence, missing receipts, workload, or an email sent outside the portal does not extend the period.

8. Case file. Mira traveled to Quarry Point, 112 road kilometers from her home but 34 road kilometers from her assigned office. She departed Monday 6 April 2026, stayed away Monday and Tuesday at midnight, and returned Wednesday 8 April. Her director pre-approved "up to 230 credits nightly at the Summit Conference Hotel and taxis up to 90 credits for the Quarry Point trip." The organizer named Summit and the block was still open when she booked at 225 credits nightly. Tuesday conference registration included breakfast. The accessibility office had documented before travel that the provided breakfast could not meet her medically required diet. A Tuesday taxi cost 82 credits; transit operated normally. Mira entered the complete claim in the portal on Monday 11 May. The portal was available throughout. Company closures in this interval were Friday 10 April and Friday 1 May.

9. Calendar note. The weekend days and the two stated closure Fridays are not business days. All other Mondays through Fridays in the interval are business days.

AMENDMENT A — adopted 15 March 2026, effective for travel beginning on or after 1 April 2026. Despite section 6, director pre-approval cannot raise the lodging cap at a named conference hotel while its conference block remains open. Such lodging is capped at the ordinary 190 credits plus separately stated taxes. The amendment does not change taxi authority or the definition of remote-site travel.

DATA ACCESS STANDARD — 2026 consolidated edition
Article 1 — Scope. This standard applies to exports from Atlas, a system containing customer contact, billing, and service telemetry. The decision is made under the version in force when access begins, except a later emergency directive expressly made immediately applicable controls ongoing access.

Article 2 — Definitions. "Direct identifier" includes name, full address, email, telephone number, account number, or any stable value that another company can use to single out a person. A hash is still a direct identifier when it is stable across exports. "Aggregate" means every released cell combines at least 25 distinct customers after all filters. "Internal research" is work performed only by employees on company-managed devices, with no external recipient or publication. A contractor is external even if issued a company email address. "Short access" lasts no more than 30 consecutive days.

Article 3 — Baseline routes. Aggregate, non-identifying data may be approved by the analytics owner. Row-level telemetry without direct identifiers requires privacy review. Any direct identifier normally requires both privacy and security review, a recorded purpose, and deletion date. Marketing consent is irrelevant to security review.

Article 4 — Academic collaboration route. A university collaborator may receive row-level telemetry stripped of direct identifiers if a data-use agreement is executed before access, the ethics approval is current, and privacy approves the transformation. The analytics owner cannot substitute for privacy. No direct identifiers may use this route.

Article 5 — Incident route. During a declared severity-one incident, the incident commander may grant engineers short access to the minimum necessary row-level data. Direct identifiers remain prohibited unless the security duty officer separately approves them. Incident access expires when the incident closes, even if 30 days have not elapsed.

Article 6 — Renewals. Renewal is a new access decision. Prior review can be relied on only if recipients, fields, purpose, environment, and transformation are unchanged. Adding a field or recipient requires the corresponding current route.

Article 7 — Case file. Aster University and the company's employee researcher plan a service-reliability study. The university agreement was signed 2 February 2026 and ethics approval runs through December. Privacy approved an export containing event time rounded to the hour, coarse three-digit postal area, device family, failure code, and `cohort_token`, described in the request as SHA-256(account_number + a secret held by the company). The same token would appear for the same account in every monthly export so longitudinal behavior can be joined. Security was copied on the request but gave no approval. The analytics owner approved it. Access is requested for 24 days. There is no declared incident. The employee says the token is anonymous because the university lacks the secret. Minimum cell size in the planned paper is 40, but the university will receive individual rows. No prior export exists.

Article 8 — Interpretation examples. A randomly regenerated token that changes independently in every export and cannot be linked by the recipient is not stable, though privacy review may still be needed for row-level data. Rounding timestamps does not make individual rows aggregate. Publication cell thresholds govern publication, not the underlying transfer.

EMERGENCY DIRECTIVE 3, issued 20 January 2026. Until withdrawn, stable hashed account values are expressly treated as direct identifiers even if the receiving party cannot reverse the hash or lacks the salt. This clarification applies immediately to new and ongoing access. Academic collaboration may not receive such values. Removal or independently randomized replacement requires a new privacy confirmation.

RECORDS DELETION AND LEGAL HOLD HANDBOOK
1. Rule hierarchy. Legal holds override ordinary deletion schedules. A later written release controls the named scope only. The privacy deletion process does not authorize destruction barred by a hold. The clarification memorandum at the end is binding.

2. Definitions. "Responsive record" means a record within the custodians, systems, subjects, and time range stated by a hold. Exact duplicates are each responsive when stored in separate systems unless the hold notice permits deduplication. "Derived analytics" are records produced from source data; they are not source records. "Verified deletion" means deletion from active systems and expiration from ordinary backups under the stated schedule, with a logged confirmation. Cryptographic erasure counts only if the relevant keys exclusively protect the named records.

3. Customer requests. A verified identity request is due within 30 calendar days. Data needed for contract performance may be retained while necessary. Data under legal hold is retained even after the ordinary purpose ends, and the customer receives the standard limitation notice. Non-held data in the same account remains subject to deletion.

4. Backup process. Active copies are deleted by the due date. Immutable backups expire on a 35-day rotation; restoration procedures must reapply deletion markers. The completion record may therefore distinguish active deletion from final backup expiry.

5. Holds. Hold H-17 covers support messages by custodians June and Omar concerning Project Cedar from 1 January through 31 March 2026, including attachments and exports. Hold H-22 covers all billing records for account 448 from 1 February onward. Neither permits deduplication. A legal email may release a hold only if it identifies the hold number and scope.

6. Case file. Account 448 submitted a verified deletion request on 6 April. Contract service ended 5 April. The account contains profile data, invoices dated February and March, support messages with June about Project Cedar dated 20 March, unrelated support messages with Omar dated 2 April, and a dashboard table derived by counting Cedar messages by week. The table contains only week and count. On 10 April Legal wrote: "Release H-17 for Omar's records only; June remains held. H-22 remains fully active." Privacy proposes deleting the profile, every support message, the derived table, and all invoices from active storage on 20 April, leaving deletion markers for backups.

7. Scope application. A release for one custodian does not release another. Records outside a hold's date range are not held merely because a named custodian created them. Derived analytics are covered only if expressly included or if they independently meet the hold's stated record description.

8. Decision options. The deletion team must choose the option that can be executed on 20 April without violating a hold. Ordinary backup expiry may follow later and does not prevent timely active-system action.

CLARIFICATION MEMORANDUM, 12 April. H-22's term "billing records" includes invoices and payment ledger entries but not profile contact fields used only for login. H-17's term "support messages" does not include aggregate derived tables that contain no message text, attachment, customer identifier, or custodian identifier. This memorandum clarifies existing scope and does not release either hold.

COMMUNITY GRANT AWARD RULEBOOK
Part 1 — Purpose and precedence. The program awards small implementation grants. Eligibility gates are applied before scoring; an ineligible application cannot win regardless of score. The board resolution at the end postdates this edition and overrides conflicting provisions.

Part 2 — Entities. An eligible lead must be a registered nonprofit or a municipal department. An unincorporated group may participate but cannot lead or receive funds. A fiscal sponsor counts as lead only if it signs the application before the deadline and accepts financial responsibility. Two entities under common control count as one applicant for the one-award limit.

Part 3 — Timing. Applications are due 17:00 local program time on 30 June. Portal receipts control. A submission may be cured within two business days only for a missing attachment that existed before the deadline; signatures, budgets, and partner commitments cannot be created during cure. A portal outage extension requires an official outage of at least 30 continuous minutes during the final two hours.

Part 4 — Budget. Requests must be 20,000 through 80,000 credits inclusive. At least 70 percent must be implementation cost. Administrative cost is any general management, accounting, rent, or fundraising amount. Equipment used directly to deliver the project is implementation. Contingency is administrative unless allocated to named implementation tasks.

Part 5 — Conflicts. A reviewer with a financial relationship to any applicant or named delivery partner must recuse. Mere residence in the served municipality is not a conflict. A recused reviewer's score is discarded, not averaged as zero.

Part 6 — Scoring. Eligible applications receive impact up to 40, feasibility up to 30, equity up to 20, and evidence up to 10. Normally the highest total wins. A proposal below 18 on feasibility cannot win. Ties are broken by higher equity, then lower requested amount.

Part 7 — Case file. Three proposals remain. Harbor Neighbors is unincorporated and lists Bright Civic Foundation as fiscal sponsor, but Bright signed at 09:00 on 1 July; Harbor's portal receipt was 29 June. It requests 40,000, with 31,000 implementation. Its valid non-conflicted scores total 91 and feasibility 27. East Ward is a municipal department, submitted on time, requests 80,000, with 55,000 named implementation equipment and work, 5,000 named implementation training, and 20,000 general administration. Its scores are impact 34, feasibility 24, equity 18, evidence 8, total 84. River Arts is a registered nonprofit under common control with last year's winning nonprofit River Center. It submitted on time, requests 62,000 with 50,000 implementation, and scores total 89 with feasibility 26. No portal outage occurred.

Part 8 — Prior awards. The ordinary one-award limit says the same applicant cannot receive awards in consecutive program years. The published FAQ once stated that separately registered affiliates are always separate; FAQs are explanatory and not amendments.

BOARD RESOLUTION 26-4, adopted 15 May. For the 2026 round only, entities under common control with a prior-year winner are eligible to apply, but their total score is reduced by six points after all reviewer-conflict adjustments. This replaces exclusion under the consecutive-year rule; it does not change the definition of common control. Also, for 2026 only, the implementation minimum is 75 percent, not 70 percent. All other gates remain.

state.request:
In PostgreSQL, list every customer exactly once with the count of that customer's paid invoices dated in 2025, including customers with zero. Tables are customers(id,name) and invoices(id,customer_id,status,issued_at). Provide one SQL query; do not use a correlated subquery.

Additional evaluation context: The report feeds a customer-retention dashboard, so absence of invoices is meaningful and must appear as a numerical zero. Assume customer IDs are unique, invoice IDs are non-null, timestamps are stored consistently, and multiple qualifying invoices may exist. The query should remain valid when the invoices table has no matching row at all. The answer will be reviewed as a complete handoff, so correctness of intermediate reasoning, units, boundary conventions, and every stated presentation constraint matters independently of whether the concluding value appears plausible.
state.response:
```sql
SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(i.id) AS paid_invoice_count
FROM customers AS c
LEFT JOIN invoices AS i ON i.customer_id = c.id
WHERE i.status = 'paid'
  AND i.issued_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
  AND i.issued_at <  DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY c.id;
```
`COUNT(i.id)` avoids counting the NULL-extended row produced by the outer join.
